title: Earl Hines's band and its alto player
summary: Handy says Hines came to hear him and tries to recall the name of Hines's violin-playing alto man.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: take me a couple of shots and I begin to call some numbers. I'll begin to blow a little bit. Take me a couple of more shots. And just give me that drum, that piano, and bass. Then I'll get the people over here. Just clap your hand, I'll bring the people here. Well around 1.30 I had Earl Hines over there, let alone all the people. Had him over there. Him and his whole band, because I know that boy was playing first alto with him, I knew him better. He's a fine guy, he played violin too.
I forget his name now, but he's a fine violin player.
Was that Donnell Howard? Would that be the point?
No, it wasn't Howard. Not in them times. Oh, I see.
No, it wasn't Mundy. I know Mundy. He was a kind of heavyset brown skinned fellow. Kind of Indian looking for him.
